content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I want to start by saying that I truly appreciate the professionalism and helpful responses in this forum. I've just completed my first basic project and have noticed that guidance on code formatting and style isn't always straightforward—even with brief articles available. Would anyone be willing to review my project and give honest feedback? I suspect it's quite detailed since I'm new to this. My experience is mostly with similar FB code like Pure Data or MaxMSP, where formatting is more automated, so adapting to [product_name] has been challenging. I'm curious about how to disable the green text in the worksheet output. I have a PDF ready to share, and I can also provide the project file if someone is interested.
Could you attach the PDF directly to your post?
Instead of focusing on font color, prioritize the clarity of your diagram. It seems you may not be aware that multiple chart sheets can be set.
Changing the text color isn't possible, but you do have control over what gets printed.

The PDF link worked as intended. My concern wasn't about the color itself, more about how it represents content—I've noticed it's shown in two areas, which can be confusing. Options relating to layout are also a bit ambiguous; there's a layout icon but no specific menu for it, which complicates the user experience. Using multiple pages seems like the way forward. I have a few questions: 1) Is it better to modularize each layout and use cut connectors, or is there a standard approach? 2) Are there any programs or PDFs you recommend that demonstrate good layout practices for complex projects? The examples I've found are quite simple. 3) Is there a way to perform an automatic cleanup or reroute connections for a selected section? Here's a related link: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users value the community’s support but are struggling with project formatting and layout customization in [company_name] tools. There is some confusion regarding visual presentation, such as text color and diagram organization, as well as missing features like automated arrangement and clearer options for layout management. Additionally, users observe several limitations in customization and best practice documentation for building larger projects.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are hoping for clearer guidelines and options on layout formatting, more flexible diagram customization (including text color changes), automated organization features, and better access to documents or examples demonstrating best practice layouts for projects.
